 November 21 ITR Deadline: Check eligibility, late fees and other important details
 Written By Bhawna Gupta Published: 11:39 AM, Nov 16, 2026 | Updated: 12:36 PM, Nov 16, 2026 The revised deadline applies to taxpayers covered under the specified audit-related provisions of Section 139(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. These generally include companies, businesses and professionals whose accounts are required to be audited under income tax rules or other applicable laws. The November 21 extension does not apply to ordinary salaried taxpayers who are not required to get their accounts audited. | ChatGPT generated/Representative Image The deadline for filing income tax returns (ITRs) for certain taxpayers is approaching. The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has extended the ITR filing deadline for Assessment Year (AY) 2026-27 from October 31 to November 21, 2026. However, this extension is not available to everyone. It mainly applies to businesses, companies and other taxpayers whose accounts are required to be audited.
 The CBDT announced the extension through Circular No. 07/2026, issued on September 28, 2026, giving eligible taxpayers an additional 21 days to file their returns.
 Who can file by November 21? 
 The revised deadline applies to taxpayers covered under the specified audit-related provisions of Section 139(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. These generally include companies, businesses and professionals whose accounts are required to be audited under income tax rules or other applicable laws.
 Partners of firms whose accounts are required to be audited are also covered. In certain cases, the extension also applies to their spouses where the relevant legal provisions are applicable.
 For example, if a business is required to get its accounts audited and its original ITR deadline was October 31, it can now file its return by November 21. However, taxpayers covered by transfer pricing provisions under Section 92E have a separate filing deadline.
 What about salaried taxpayers? 
 The November 21 extension does not apply to ordinary salaried taxpayers who are not required to get their accounts audited. It also does not automatically apply to pensioners and other individuals filing returns without an audit requirement.
 Their regular filing deadlines are separate and are not changed by this particular CBDT circular. This distinction is important because some taxpayers may assume that the government has extended the ITR filing deadline for everyone. The extension is specifically meant for the categories mentioned in the CBDT's notification.
 Tax audit deadline also extended 
 Along with the income tax return filing deadline, the CBDT also extended the deadline for submitting tax audit reports. The earlier deadline for furnishing the tax audit report was September 30, 2026. It was extended to October 21, 2026, for the specified category of taxpayers.
 This means the extended audit report deadline has already passed, while the ITR filing deadline is November 21.
 Taxpayers covered by the extension should ensure that their audit reports have been submitted and their income details are properly reflected in their returns.
 What happens if you miss November 21? 
 Taxpayers who fail to file their returns by the applicable deadline may still be able to submit a belated return. For AY 2026-27, the deadline for filing a belated return is December 31, 2026, or before completion of assessment, whichever is earlier. However, late filing may attract additional charges.
 Under Section 234F, the late filing fee can be up to Rs 5,000. For taxpayers whose total income does not exceed Rs 5 lakh, the fee is limited to Rs 1,000. Interest on unpaid tax may also apply, depending on the circumstances. Late filing can also affect the ability to carry forward certain losses to future years.
 How to file your ITR? 
 Eligible taxpayers can file their income tax returns through the official e-filing portal at www.incometax.gov.in . Before filing, they should check their income details, tax deducted at source (TDS), advance tax payments and other relevant information.
 Businesses and professionals should also ensure that their financial statements and audit reports are in order. After submitting the return, taxpayers should complete the required verification process.
 Why is the deadline important? 
 The November 21 extension provides additional time to taxpayers whose returns involve audited accounts and detailed financial information. However, with the deadline approaching, eligible taxpayers should complete their filing process rather than leave it until the last day.
 They should also confirm that the extension applies to their category, as the revised deadline does not cover every income tax return filer.
